title: 7. Second Council of Nicaea (787)
about: The holy icons: why we venerate images of Christ and His saints.

items.text: From 726 emperors of the iconoclast party ordered icons destroyed, calling them idols. Monks and laypeople suffered for them. In 787 the Empress Irene called a council at Nicaea.

God commanded golden cherubim over the ark. The unseen God has shown Himself: 'he who has seen Me has seen the Father'. Christ, the image of the invisible God, can be painted because He truly became man.

days.title: The honour passes to the prototype

items.text: The council quoted St Basil: 'the honour paid to the image passes to its prototype'. Find the words in On the Holy Spirit, chapter 18.

items.father: St Basil the Great, On the Holy Spirit, chapter 18
St John of Damascus on images (Exposition, Book 4, chapter 16)

items.text: The council distinguished worship (latreia), due to God alone, from veneration (proskynesis) given to icons, the Cross, the Gospel book and relics. It also gave 22 canons.
After a second wave of iconoclasm, icons were restored for good in 843. The Church keeps this every year on the first Sunday of Great Lent, the Sunday of Orthodoxy, with a procession of icons.
These are the Epistle and Gospel read on the Sunday of Orthodoxy.
